title: Security & Compliance Integrated Playbook: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency & Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, Risk Exceptions
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose
This playbook provides an integrated reference for Security and Compliance practices that must be applied across Redwood Inference: RBAC and authentication, audit logging and retention, data residency and retention requirements, secure SDLC checkpoints, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and the risk & exceptions process. It is intended for service owners, platform engineers, security reviewers, and compliance owners.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood-managed services and customer-facing environments (hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Includes control ownership, required artifacts, operational thresholds, and approval workflows.

1) RBAC & Authentication (Design and Operational Controls)
Overview:
- enforce least-privilege across all services; prefer role-based groups over individual grants.
- All interactive access must be SSO-enabled (SAML/OIDC) with enforced MFA.
- Service-to-service auth must use short-lived mTLS tokens or workload identity (OIDC) where available.

Required Roles and Minimum Privileges:
- platform-admin: full ctl-plane access; restricted to 5 named personnel; require 2FA + hardware token for account elevation.
- infra-ops: create/modify infra resources (IAM, networking) but no access to customer data stores.
- svc-account: scoped to a single service, rotated credentials every 30 days (automated).
- dev-readonly: read-only access to infra and logs; used for debugging without change privileges.
- security-auditor: access to audit logs and evidence bundles; read-only.

RBAC Standards (must be implemented for every service):
1. All roles defined in a central IAM catalog (location: /infra/iam/role-catalog).
2. Role bindings declared as code (policy-as-code) in repository and reviewed via PR.
3. All changes to role bindings require approval from owner and security reviewer.
4. Default service accounts disabled; explicit creation via IaC only.

Authentication & Provisioning:
- SSO configured via corporate IdP (Okta). SCIM provisioning required for team lifecycle automation.
- Break-glass accounts: logged, time-limited (max 8 hours), and require post-use justification.

Audit & Access Review:
- Quarterly access reviews for all high-privilege roles. Owner must attest via the access-review dashboard.
- Automated alerts for anomalous privilege changes (threshold: >2 changes to same role in 24h).

2) Audit Logging (Collection, Retention, Monitoring)
Logging Requirements:
- Audit events required: authentication events, role changes, policy modifications, data access to customer data stores, admin console actions, and service account key creation.
- All audit streams centralized to the Security Logging Cluster and immutable storage (WORM bucket) for legal retention.

Minimum Log Schema (must be present in each event):
- timestamp, principal, action, resource, outcome (success/fail), request_id, source_ip, region, service_version.

Retention & Storage Table:
- Purpose: ensure compliance with internal policy and legal obligations.

| Artifact Type                 | Short-term Storage (hot) | Archive (cold)     | Retention Period |
|------------------------------|--------------------------|--------------------|------------------|
| Authentication logs          | 90 days                  | WORM archive       | 7 years          |
| Admin & role-change logs     | 365 days                 | WORM archive       | 7 years          |
| Customer data access logs    | 2 years                  | WORM archive       | 7 years or per customer agreement |
| Application traces & metrics | 90 days                  | 3 years            | 3 years          |

Retention Exceptions:
- Any deviation requires a documented exception and approval (see Risk & Exceptions).

Monitoring & Alerting:
- Baseline: forward error-rate and anomalous auth patterns into SIEM with these alert thresholds:
  - >5 failed login attempts per account within 5 minutes: P2 alert.
  - Privilege escalation event on a production role: P1 alert.
  - Data export operation > 100MB to external endpoint: P1 alert.
- Use playbooks in section 5 for automated triage.

3) Data Residency & Data Retention (Customer Data Handling)
Policy Summary:
- Customer data must remain in the region(s) contracted in the customer agreement. Default: US and EU regions only.
- Backup copies must follow the same residency constraints.
- Metadata and telemetry that do not contain PII can be global unless customer opts out.

Data Classification & Handling Requirements:
- PII/Customer Confidential: encrypted at rest with CMEK/HSM; access logged and limited to named roles.
- Aggregated telemetry: pseudonymized and stored per product policy.

Retention Requirements (per data class):
- Customer raw inputs/outputs: default retention 30 days for hosted API, configurable by customer up to contractual limits.
- Billing and invoice records: 7 years.
- Audit/evidence artifacts: see section 6.

Cross-border Transfer Controls:
- Transfers require documented legal basis and DPA clauses; consult Legal before enabling cross-border replication for customer data.

4) Secure SDLC (Gates, Tooling, and Responsibilities)
SDLC Gate Summary:
- Security must be integrated into every stage: design, implementation, testing, and release. The pipeline must enforce automated checks and manual approvals where needed.

Required Controls by Stage:
1. Design: Threat model and data flow diagrams for all new services/features; approved by security lead.
2. Implement: Static Application Security Testing (SAST) on PR; dependency scanning with CVE policy (block high/critical unpatched dependencies).
3. Build/Test: Secrets scanning; container image scanning; SBOM generation for production images.
4. Pre-Release: DAST/penetration testing for major features and public endpoints; staging security smoke tests.
5. Release: Security sign-off required for production deploys affecting auth/data paths.

Checklist for Release Approval (sample):
- Threat model updated and reviewed.
- SAST score within threshold or risk accepted with mitigation.
- No critical/high open CVEs in production deps.
- Secrets disclosure check passed.
- Security reviewer approval recorded in PR.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures (CI/CD and Production Incidents)
Overview:
- This section complements the company incident process with security-specific actions for incidents affecting confidentiality, integrity, or availability of customer data or controls.

Initial Triage (first 60 minutes):
1. Triage owner (security on-call) acknowledges within 15 minutes.
2. Classify: data breach, unauthorized privilege change, service compromise, or other.
3. Preserve artifacts: snapshot logs, capture memory if live, freeze relevant IAM changes.
4. Contain: rotate affected keys, revoke compromised sessions, isolate affected hosts or services.

Forensic & Evidence Preservation:
- All steps must be logged, and copies of artifacts stored in the forensics bucket (WORM) with tamper-evident metadata.
- Maintain chain-of-custody record (CSV template included below).

Communication & Escalation:
- P1 (customer data exfiltration or production compromise): page Security, SRE, Legal, and Product; run incident war-room.
- Notify CISO and CEO within 1 hour for P1 incidents.
- External communications (customers, regulators, press) must be routed through Legal and Communications.

Post-Incident Activities:
- Postmortem within 7 business days, including root cause, remediation plan, and evidence attachments.
- Follow-up audit to confirm remediation with owners and deadlines.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows (Artifact Collection & Audit Readiness)
Evidence Catalog (examples):
- Identity proofs: SCIM/audit logs showing provisioning dates.
- RBAC proofs: IAM policy snapshots and PR history.
- Audit logs: WORM access logs, SIEM export with retention proof.
- SDLC proofs: SAST/DAST report snapshots, SBOM artifacts, pen test reports.

Evidence Storage & Access:
- Evidence bundles are stored in the Compliance Evidence Repository (CER) with tags: control-id, owner, period. Access limited to security-auditor and legal.

Audit Preparation Procedure (quarterly or on-demand):
1. Control owner runs evidence collection script to bundle artifacts into CER.
2. Security reviewer verifies artifact integrity and completeness.
3. Legal compiles audit package and coordinates external auditor access.
4. All evidence must include metadata: created_by, created_at, checksum, retention_policy.

7) Risk & Exceptions Process
When to Request an Exception:
- Temporary operational needs (e.g., emergency debug requiring extended retention).
- New product requirements that conflict with a standing security control.

Exception Request Workflow (required fields):
- requester, service impacted, control being excepted, justification, proposed compensating controls, duration (max 90 days for short-term exceptions), business owner, security reviewer.

Approvals:
- Low-risk exceptions: Security lead + Service owner.
- High-risk or permanent exceptions: CISO + Legal + CTO.
- All exceptions are logged in the Risk Register and have an explicit review date.

Periodic Review:
- All exceptions reviewed at 30/60/90-day intervals; renewals require reapproval and a documented remediation roadmap.

Appendices
A. Artifact Templates
- Chain-of-custody CSV header: artifact_id, collector, timestamp_utc, location, original_checksum, comment
- Exception request template: requester, date, service, control, risk_level, compensating_controls, approval_chain

Usage Notes
- This is an organizational policy reference. Service teams must implement these controls in their service README and IaC. Exceptions must be documented and approved prior to production deviations.
